ranked_evidence.title: CJP's parliament march from Jantar Mantar: India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown - BBC
ranked_evidence.snippet: # India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown. Thousands have gathered again in the Indian capital Delhi a day after a police crackdown on supporters of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement seeking education reforms and resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Tens of thousands of young men and women had turned up for Monday's protest and tried to march on parliament, defying a police ban. Police said 118 of their personnel were also injured and 70 protesters have been detained. Police and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government have not commented on the use of sticks and tear gas against protesters. The meeting took place against the backdrop of tens of thousands of people turning up from all over the country to participate in the CJP's call to march to parliament on the opening day of the monsoon session.

ranked_evidence.title: Indian police forcibly hospitalize a prominent Cockroach Party activist on hunger strike - NBC News
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Indian police forcibly hospitalize a prominent Cockroach Party activist on hunger strike. Police said activist Sonam Wangchuk was taken to hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike, and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party movement for education reform. Authorities tightened security around New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, a designated public protest ground enclosed by police barricades, where activist Sonam Wangchuk has been camped along with students and Cockroach Party activists who demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, after allegations that exam papers were leaked in advance. Delhi Police said Wangchuk was taken to hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike, and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move.

ranked_evidence.title: Indian police forcibly hospitalize Cockroach Janata Party activist on hunger strike - Los Angeles Times
ranked_evidence.snippet: * Police in New Delhi forcibly moved education reform activist Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike. NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s Cockroach Janata Party movement for education reform. Delhi police said that Wangchuk was taken to the hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. The Cockroach Janata Party — a play on the name of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party — said in a social media post that the government “forcefully abducted” Wangchuk “without his or his family’s consent” two days before their planned march to India’s Parliament.

ranked_evidence.title: India's cockroach protests: Modi breaks silence and hunger strike ends | BBC News - Modern Ghana
ranked_evidence.snippet: # India's cockroach protests: Modi breaks silence and hunger strike ends | BBC News. Thousands of people continue to protest demanding the Indian education minister's resignation after representatives of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held talks with the government. The meeting came after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his hunger strike after 26 days of fasting in solidarity with the protests. A CJP spokesperson told reporters that the government has asked for a day to decide on their biggest demand - minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also spoken, posted a video promising a tough new law on examination paper leaks, the issue at the core of the protests.
